Committee on Health and Human Services Re: LD 70 - An Act to Fund Free Health Clinics
March 13, 2025
Dear Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and distinguished members of the Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Gia Drew and I am the Executive Director of EqualityMaine, which has been advocating on behalf of Maine's LGBTQ+ community since 1984. We urge you to support LD 70 in order to ensure all Mainers have access to healthcare and can move across boundaries to care.
Across the state, and in seven different counties, there are approximately eight free healthcare clinics operating independently or with other organizations servicing thousands of patients a year,1 though not all receive funding from the state. Patients accessing these services are largely low-income who are at or below 200% poverty level and have high deductible insurance or none at all2. These marginalized groups may only be accessing care through these free clinics, due to their physical proximity, making them essential and causing stress when these services are not available.
LGBTQ+ people experience even higher levels of stress as outlined by the social determinants of health. These are non-medical factors that affect mental and physical health at higher rates over the span of someone's life like anti-LGBTQ+ policy, discrimination, violence, or a hostile climate. Stemming from this stress, LGBTQ+ populations face higher rates of mental and physical health disparities, and on top of this, 21% of LGBTQ+ people also experience poverty at a higher rate than non-LGBTQ+ people3. This rate of poverty combined with a higher likelihood of mental and physical health issues makes free healthcare clinics even more necessary and beneficial to the community.
In 2023 alone, there was an 80% increase in patient demand, making clinics more needed than ever.4 Research also shows that the cost of operating these healthcare clinics has risen

in the past 20 years. While this bill proposes that the state allocate $250,000 to the clinics in Maine, in 2019 the average operating cost of a free clinic was $387,252.5 Additionally, for certain services people may have to pay a small fee. Thus, we propose that the allocation of funds be increased to account for inflation, rising operating costs and patient demand, and for the benefit of people in Mainer accessing these services who deserve to do so with as few barriers as possible.
According to a study on the expansion of access to free clinics, long patient wait-times, which are standard for free health clinics, can impact patient satisfaction and decrease the number of patients a provider can see in a day.6 This furthers health disparities by discouraging a patient from coming back to the clinic, which can lead to misdiagnosis, miscommunications, and inconsistency, adding to stressors patients already experience on a day-to-day basis. By increasing funding, a clinic can hire more providers, expanding the number of people they care for in addition to offering more jobs for a community and developing better patient care and satisfaction.
The impact that free health clinics have on vulnerable communities is immense and can often be immediate. A trip to the free clinic for an uninsured or low-income person may just save their life. We ask you to vote "ought to pass" on LD 70 to ensure that people in Maine have access to the care they need. Healthcare is a human right and as providers are seeing an increase in demand, there has never been a more critical time to invest in Maine's healthcare system.
Thank you,
Gia Drew (she/her) Executive Director, EqualityMaine

Testimony ofRepresentative Michael Brennan presenting
LD 70, An Act to Fund Free Health Clinics
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
Good aftemoon, Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and distinguished members of the
Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services. My name is Michael Bren-nan, and I
represent House District 115, which includes a portion of Portland.
I want to thank my House colleague for reading this testimony and presenting LD 70 on my
behalf. I apologize that I cannot be with you in person today.
LD 70 is a bill that has been before this committee for at least the last two sessions. The bill was
funded two years ago, and following an unfortunate delay, the funds were awarded. Last year, the bill was voted off the Appropriations Table to be funded at $100,000. However, it was one of the bills on the final day of the session that died.
This bill provides one-time funding of $250,000 for Maine's free health clinics. At last count, there were five free clinics in the state. The funding is to be distributed based on a formula
adopted by the Department of Health and Human Services, using the number of clients sewed
and a base amount of funding for each clinic.
Members of this committee are aware of the struggle too many people in Maine have in finding health care. The Portland Free Clinic provides primary health care to over 500 people for under
$250,000 a year. Physicians, nurses, social workers and other health care professionals donate their expertise to assist clients of the clinic. This modest amount of state funds will support their work and assist hundreds of Maine residents.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to seeing you at the work session.

District 115: Part of Portland
